title: Instant API Hello: Hosted UX + Pricing Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick, experiment-ready messaging and microcopy for a developer-first hosted API quickstart that emphasizes time-to-first-inference, cost clarity, and predictable progression from trial to production. This is a working doc — keep short snippets, A/B variants, and tactical TODOs.

Constraints & guiding principles:
- Developer-first language: assume engineer doing the integration. Keep copy terse, concrete, example-driven.
- Time-to-value claims must be conservative and measurable (validate with telemetry). Proposed baseline: "first inference in < 60s" across demo templates.
- Pricing language must reduce fear: show per-call cost examples and one clear production path (pay-as-you-go -> reserved).
- Provide fallback language for security-conscious buyers (private/dedicated mentions).

Core value props (short bullets for UI and hero lines):
- "Run high-throughput inference with predictable latency and transparent costs."
- "Get a working call in under a minute — sample code, sample model, sample data."
- "Ship confidently: rollout controls, canaries, and model fallbacks built-in."
- "Lower unit cost with smart batching and caching — we surface savings suggestions."

Onboarding microflows to emphasize in-copy:
1) Try: "Paste your prompt, see a reply" — no signup friction for playground sample.
2) Integrate: 3 lines of code in README -> first token streamed back.
3) Scale: show how to reserve capacity or enable autoscaling.

Quickstart code snippets (for docs + SDK README) — keep minimal and language-agnostic:
- HTTP (curl) example to use in hero and playbook:
  curl \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{"model":"rwd-compact-1","input":"Summarize: Our quarterly plan"}' \\n    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/outputs

- Node (1-file) example for README:
  const client = require('@redwood/infer');
  const r = new client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
  await r.outputs.create({ model: 'rwd-compact-1', input: 'Hello world' });

Headline A/B copy candidates:
A1: "From first call to production — fast, predictable LLM inference."
A2: "Deploy LLM features with measured latency and transparent unit costs."
B1: "Your first inference in under a minute — code + sample data included."
B2: "Try a sample call, then scale with reserved capacity and SLAs."

Pricing language experiments (UI copy + examples):
- Goal: reduce sticker shock; show small, relatable examples.
- Anchor with a tiny concrete example near price table: "1 short chat = ~0.5¢; 1k chats ≈ $5".
- Variant phrasing:
  V1 (simple): "Pay-as-you-go: per-token billing with transparent estimates in the console."
  V2 (progressive): "Starter: meter per 1k tokens. Grow: reserve capacity for predictable monthly spend."
  V3 (cost-reassure): "We surface estimated token usage and cost before you send large batches."
- Bundles / productized steps to test:
  - Starter credits (30 days): $50 credit on sign-up for new projects.
  - Predictable band: reserve a small GPU pool for a month, get a flat rate for X tokens/day.
  - Burst allowance: temporary extra throughput on top of reserved capacity.

Pricing UI copy snippets:
- CTA: "Estimate cost for this payload" (button next to playground).
- Tooltip: "Estimate computed from sample prompt and model; actual usage may vary."
- Meter label: "tokens / 1k" or "embeddings per 10k vectors" depending on endpoint.

Competitive angle notes (fast bullets for pitch deck):
- Against managed cloud endpoints: we emphasize developer ergonomics + production controls (rollouts, token breakdown, per-route tracing) rather than just raw VM scaling.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: we push the "one API across hosted/dedicated/private" story — same SDK, same routing and observability.
- Against API-first LLM vendors: price clarity and unit-cost tooling (batch/caching recommendations) are differentiators — call these out in a feature row.
- Quick objection answers:
  Q: "I can self-host cheaper." A: "Possibly at scale — but we stop the trial/ops tax: day-1 integration, telemetry, and incremental commitments for predictable spend."
  Q: "How does cost work for embeddings?" A: "Metering per vector batch, example estimate shown alongside embedding playground."

UX experiments to run (quick A/B matrix):
1) Playground CTA wording: "Try a live call" vs "Run a sample inference" — measure click-to-first-API-call time and conversion to API key.
2) Pricing anchor: show per-call micro-example vs. per-1k-token table — measure perceived affordability in intercept survey.
3) Credit offer layout: $50 in a banner vs. $50 on the billing page — measure redemption and downstream usage.
4) Console estimator utility: inline estimator vs. separate estimator page — measure estimator engagement and demo-to-paid conversion.

Microcopy bank (ready-to-use snippets):
- Onboarding step: "Grab an API key — paste into your app — send your first request."
- Billing banner: "Start with $50 free credit — no card for 14 days." (experiment: remove "no card").
- Capacity CTA: "Reserve predictable capacity" (link to Dedicated product flow).

Measurement and success criteria:
- SLAs: track how many quickstarts reach a first successful inference within 60s of landing on quickstart page. Target: 65% within 60s in the first month.
- Pricing clarity: post-conversion survey question — "Did the pricing examples help you estimate cost?" target: 70% yes.
- CTO/Platform interest: # of early inbound leads who request dedicated/private after hitting usage threshold. Target: 10 in quarter.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get a validated telemetry number for median quickstart time (engineering).
- Legal: confirm we can use small monetary examples (e.g., ¢ per chat) in public docs.
- Design: create small estimator component for playground (desktop + mobile).
- Content: finalize hero microcopy variants and run internal vote.

Next steps (owners):
- Marco: wireframe playground estimator + CTA variants (deadline: 2024-11-20).
- Lina: coordinate with billing team on starter credit copy & promo mechanics (2024-11-18).
- Priya: run 2 internal A/B variants on headline copy and report conversion delta (2024-11-22).

Notes to reviewers: this doc is tactical — please add microcopy tweaks inline, flag any claims that require product/legal sign-off, and list other pricing permutations you've seen in competitor sites.
